title: Given a string of only '(' and ')', return the length of the longest substring that is a valid (well-formed) parentheses sequence.
shortTitle: Longest Valid Parentheses — longest balanced substring

s1_definition.profdef: Solvable by a stack of indices seeded with a sentinel −1: push indices of '(', and on ')' pop; if the stack becomes empty push the current index as a new base, otherwise the valid length is current index minus the new stack top. Track the maximum. Time O(n), space O(n). A DP and an O(1)-space two-pass also exist.
s1_definition.analogy: A message-framing checker at National Bank of India finds the longest stretch of a protocol string where every open marker is properly closed. It remembers the position just before each unmatched point and measures balanced runs from there.
s1_definition.oneliner: Stack of indices with a −1 base; on ')' pop and measure current − new top; track max.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Solvable by a stack of indices seeded with a sentinel −1: push indices of '(', and on ')' pop; if the stack becomes empty push the current index as a new base, otherwise the valid length is current index minus the new stack top. Track the maximum. Time O(n), space O(n). A DP and an O(1)-space two-pass also exist.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** A message-framing checker at National Bank of India finds the longest stretch of a protocol string where every open marker is properly closed. It remembers the position just before each unmatched point and measures balanced runs from there.

**One line to remember:** Stack of indices with a −1 base; on ')' pop and measure current − new top; track max.

sections.s2_technical:
Use a stack holding indices, initialized with −1 as a base marker meaning "the position just before a valid run." For each open parenthesis, push its index. For each close parenthesis, pop the top. After popping, if the stack is now empty, this close has no match, so push the current index as a new base. If the stack is not empty, the top is the index just before the current valid run, so the valid length is the current index minus that top. For example: `stack.pop(); if (stack.isEmpty()) stack.push(i); else best = Math.max(best, i - stack.peek());`.

The sentinel −1 is the elegance: it lets the very first valid run be measured without special casing, since a run ending at index i that started at the beginning has length i minus negative one.

The time is O(n) and space is O(n). A senior nuance is the constant-space two-pass alternative: scan left to right counting opens and closes and record the length when they balance, resetting when closes exceed opens, then do the same right to left; this avoids the stack entirely.
sections.s3_banking:
Problem 1 — At National Bank of India, a protocol parser must find the longest well-framed stretch of a message where every open marker has a matching close, to isolate the largest intact segment after corruption. This is exactly how Longest Valid Parentheses works.

Problem 2 — Simply counting balanced markers is not enough because the valid part must be contiguous. This is exactly why index positions are tracked on a stack with a base sentinel.

The mini-project builds a `MessageFramer`, a `BankLogFormatter`, and a runnable demo.

sections.s5_journey:
The input string is close, open, close, open, close, close.

Step 1: The stack starts with the sentinel minus one.

Step 2: The first close pops the sentinel, leaving the stack empty, so index zero becomes the new base.

Step 3: An open pushes its index, a close pops it, and the valid length is measured from the base, giving two.

Step 4: Another open and close extend the balanced run to length four measured from the base at index zero.

Step 5: The final unmatched close becomes a new base, and the maximum stays four, while the string open-open-close gives two.

```text
2026-10-27T05:10:00Z [INFO] National Bank of India — Message Framer (Longest Valid Parentheses)
2026-10-27T05:10:00Z [INFO] Longest valid parentheses = 4
2026-10-27T05:10:00Z [INFO] ')()())' → 4
2026-10-27T05:10:00Z [INFO] Longest valid parentheses = 2
2026-10-27T05:10:00Z [INFO] '(()' → 2
```
sections.s5b_flow:
```text
  s = ) ( ) ( ) )
  stack=[-1]
  i0 ')': pop→empty, push 0        stack=[0]
  i1 '(': push 1                   stack=[0,1]
  i2 ')': pop→ top0, len=2-0=2 ... best=2
  i3 '(': push 3                   stack=[0,3]
  i4 ')': pop→ top0, len=4-0=4 ... best=4
  i5 ')': pop→empty, push 5        stack=[5]
  answer = 4
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Longest Valid Parentheses asks for the longest contiguous well-formed substring, and my preferred solution uses a stack of indices seeded with a sentinel of minus one. The sentinel represents the position just before a valid run. For each open parenthesis I push its index, and for each close parenthesis I pop the top.

After popping, there are two cases. If the stack is now empty, this close had no matching open, so I push its own index as a new base for future runs. If the stack is not empty, the new top is the index just before the current valid run, so the valid length is the current index minus that top, and I keep the maximum. The sentinel minus one is the elegance, because it lets a valid run that starts at the very beginning be measured without any special casing.

In my project at National Bank of India, a protocol parser had to find the longest well-framed stretch of a message where every open marker had a matching close, to isolate the largest intact segment after corruption. Because the valid part must be contiguous, simply counting balanced markers is not enough, so I tracked index positions on the stack, and I mention the constant-space two-pass counting alternative as a follow-up.
